overview.heading: How the Wedding Invitation Maker works
paragraphs: Enter the couple's names, the date, the venue and, if you wish, the time, the city and an RSVP line. Choose an opening line, an invitation line and a style, and PiCraft designs a complete portrait invitation in the proportions of a 5×7 inch card.

By default the card uses a traditional wedding wording: "Together with their families" at the top and "request the pleasure of your company at their wedding" before the date. Two drop-downs change those lines. The opening line can be "Together with their parents", "With joyful hearts" or left out, and the invitation line can be "request the honor of your presence at their wedding", "invite you to celebrate their wedding" or "are getting married". Your names, date, time, venue, city and RSVP line are set into the wording you choose and spelled exactly as you typed them.
You download a print PDF with 0.125 inch bleed for a printer, a 300 DPI JPG of the same file, and a phone-sized image for text messages, WhatsApp and email.

whatYouGet.title: Print PDF with bleed
whatYouGet.description: A 5×7 inch invitation with 0.125 inch bleed on every side at 300 DPI, ready to send to a print shop.

whatYouGet.title: Print JPG at 300 DPI
whatYouGet.description: The same print file as a JPG for services and home printers that prefer images.

whatYouGet.title: A 1080×1500 px share image
whatYouGet.description: A version sized for phones, to send in text messages, chats, email or an Instagram story.

whatYouGet.title: Ten wedding styles
whatYouGet.description: Watercolor botanical, modern minimal, classic gold, boho arch, Art Deco, beach and more.

whatYouGet.title: Your details already typeset
whatYouGet.description: Names, date, time, venue, city and RSVP are laid out with a clear hierarchy, with no template to edit.

useCases.title: Formal printed invitations
useCases.description: Send the PDF to a local printer or an online print service and choose a heavy card stock.

useCases.title: Digital-first weddings
useCases.description: Share the phone-sized image by message or email when you want to invite people quickly.

useCases.title: Destination weddings
useCases.description: Send a digital invitation early so guests can plan travel, followed by printed cards for close family.

useCases.title: Engagement parties and showers
useCases.description: Reuse the same style with different wording for the events around the wedding.

useCases.title: Save-the-date style cards
useCases.description: Generate a simple card with the names, date and city, and use the RSVP line for your website.

tips.title: Write names the way you want them printed
tips.description: Use first names or full names, with "&" or "and". The card copies whatever you type.

tips.title: Spell out the date in full
tips.description: "Saturday, June 12, 2027" is clear and formal. Add the time on its own line instead of in the date.

tips.title: Keep the venue to one line
tips.description: Use the venue name in the venue field and put the city in its own field. Long addresses crowd the card.

tips.title: Put your website in the RSVP line
tips.description: A line such as "Kindly reply by May 1 · emmaandjames.com" saves room for the details on a wedding website.

tips.title: Read the lines as one sentence
tips.description: The opening line, your names and the invitation line read as a single sentence, such as "Together with their parents Emma Collins & James Porter invite you to celebrate their wedding". Say it aloud before you generate.

tips.title: Choose a style that matches the venue
tips.description: Botanical and rustic suit gardens and barns, Art Deco suits city ballrooms, beach suits the coast.

tips.title: Generate more than once
tips.description: Each attempt is a new design. Try a few and keep the one where the layout and the artwork feel right.

tips.title: Proofread twice
tips.description: Have a second person read every name, date and time. A typo in a name is the one mistake you cannot reprint around.

styleGuide.heading: Choosing a wedding style
styleGuide.intro: The style sets the artwork, the lettering and the feeling of the invitation.

items.title: Watercolor botanical
items.description: Soft painted leaves and flowers. Fits spring and summer weddings, gardens and greenhouses.

items.title: Modern minimal
items.description: Plenty of space, simple type and a quiet palette. Fits city weddings and contemporary venues.

items.title: Classic gold
items.description: Traditional layout with gold accents. Fits formal ceremonies and ballroom receptions.

items.title: Boho arch
items.description: Earth tones and arch shapes. Fits relaxed outdoor weddings.

items.title: Romantic garden
items.description: Lush florals with a soft palette. Fits garden parties and estate venues.

items.title: Art Deco
items.description: Geometric patterns and metallic lines. Fits [glamorous evening weddings](/create/wedding-invitation-maker/art-deco).

items.title: Rustic wood
items.description: Natural textures and warm tones. Fits barns, farms and woodland venues.

items.title: Beach & coastal
items.description: Sea colors and light patterns. Fits [seaside and island weddings](/create/wedding-invitation-maker/beach).

items.title: Moody & dark
items.description: Deep colors and rich florals. Fits autumn and winter evening weddings.

items.title: Cherry blossom
items.description: Pink blossoms and gentle watercolor. Fits spring weddings and garden venues.

checklist.heading: Before you print the invitations
items: Check both names, the date, the day of the week, the time and the venue against your booking.
Have a second person read the invitation aloud.
Confirm your RSVP deadline and website address are correct.
Ask your printer for a paper proof, or order one test copy, before a full order.
Tell the printer the finished size is 5×7 inches with 0.125 inch bleed, and ask for trim to 5×7.
Choose a heavy card stock, 110 lb (300 gsm) or more, for a premium feel.
Order A7 envelopes, which fit a 5×7 inch card.

limits: The wording comes from two short lists, four opening lines and four invitation lines, and is in English. For any other phrasing, use the RSVP line or add text in an editor.
It does not add a photo of the couple, a monogram or a map.
Names with unusual spellings or accents should be checked closely, because AI text rendering is not perfect.
Matching items such as RSVP cards, menus and place cards are separate designs and will not be identical in style.
The text is part of the image. To change a word, generate again.
